# prism-curate Specification

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json. Change the app through your agent with /prism, not by editing this file. -->

## Purpose

Prism Curate: Decides whether one candidate set of a facet's tunable parameters, a deterministic Rule-30 hypothesis or the observer's reconciliation toward the owner, replaces the parameters the facet runs now: adopt it under a new kappa-named claim, recall it under a claim already made, keep what runs, or refuse. A candidate is adopted only with zero humane defects, on the owner's own gestures, without falling below the facet's floor, and only when it Pareto-dominates what runs (a hypothesis) or eases the owner's dismissals (a reconciliation).

## Requirements

### Requirement: Always refuse when halted is yes

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when halted is yes, because the kill switch stops curation: nothing is adopted while halted.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-001, theorem `inv001Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-001 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `yes yes admit zero owner kept explore yes dominates new` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: Always refuse when tunable is no

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when tunable is no, because a parameter the spec does not mark tunable, or a value off its step or bounds, is never set.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-002, theorem `inv002Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-002 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `no no admit zero owner kept explore yes dominates new` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: Always refuse when label is other

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when label is other, because every adoption is named by a kappa label the kappa facet admitted.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-003, theorem `inv003Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-003 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `no yes other zero owner kept explore yes dominates new` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: Never adopt when defect is some

The app SHALL NOT answer `adopt` when defect is some, because the humane gate: a candidate with any defect is never adopted (defect = 0).

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-004, theorem `inv004Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-004 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `no yes admit some owner kept explore yes dominates new` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `adopt`
- **AND** the app answers `keep`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: The first matching rule decides

The app SHALL try REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-011 in that order, and the first rule that matches SHALL decide.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: Two rules match

- **WHEN** the request is `no yes admit zero owner kept explore yes dominates known` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `recall`, decided by REQ-010, the earlier rule

### Requirement: Request and answers

The app SHALL read one request as one line of 10 fields separated by single spaces, in this order, and SHALL answer exactly one of `adopt`, `recall`, `keep`, `refuse`, or `invalid` for anything else.

| Field | Accepts | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `halted` | `no`, `yes` | whether the owner pressed the kill switch |
| `tunable` | `yes`, `no` | whether every parameter the candidate sets is one the facet's spec marks tunable, on its step and within its bounds |
| `label` | `admit`, `other` | the kappa facet's answer on the candidate's claim label (admit), or any other answer |
| `defect` | `zero`, `some` | the candidate's humane defects on replay of the window: answers that break a guarantee of the facet's spec |
| `evidence` | `owner`, `self` | whether the window the candidate was replayed on holds at least the minimum of the owner's own gestures |
| `floor` | `kept`, `regressed` | whether the facet's floor Pareto-dominates the candidate (regressed) or not (kept) |
| `move` | `explore`, `reconcile` | whether the candidate is a Rule-30 hypothesis (explore) or the observer's reconciliation (reconcile): the one step of one tunable that most lowers the owner's dismissals on replay |
| `eased` | `yes`, `no` | whether the candidate, on replay, brings forward fewer items the owner dismissed than what runs |
| `dominance` | `dominates`, `equal`, `dominated`, `incomparable` | the candidate against what runs, on the facet's objectives (each minimized): no worse on all and better on one, the same on all, no better on all and worse on one, or neither |
| `claim` | `new`, `known` | whether the candidate's claim label is already in the facet's ledger |

| Answer | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `adopt` | the candidate runs, under a new kappa-named claim |
| `recall` | the candidate runs, under a claim already made |
| `keep` | what runs now stays |
| `refuse` | the candidate is never weighed |
| `invalid` | the request is malformed |

Verified: reading a request is tested, not proved.

#### Scenario: A malformed request is invalid

- **WHEN** the request is not 10 fields in this order
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `invalid`

## Examples

- `no yes admit zero owner kept explore yes dominates new` gives `adopt`
- `no yes admit zero owner kept explore yes dominates known` gives `recall`
- `no yes admit zero owner kept explore yes equal new` gives `keep`
- `no yes admit zero owner kept explore yes dominated new` gives `keep`
- `no yes admit zero owner kept explore yes incomparable new` gives `keep`
- `no yes admit zero owner kept reconcile yes incomparable new` gives `adopt`
- `no yes admit zero owner kept reconcile yes dominated known` gives `recall`
- `no yes admit zero owner kept reconcile no dominates new` gives `keep`
- `no yes admit zero owner regressed reconcile yes dominates new` gives `keep`
- `no yes admit zero self kept explore yes dominates new` gives `keep`
- `no yes admit some owner kept explore yes dominates new` gives `keep`
- `no yes other zero owner kept explore yes dominates new` gives `refuse`
- `no no admit zero owner kept explore yes dominates new` gives `refuse`
- `yes yes admit zero owner kept explore yes dominates new` gives `refuse`
- `no yes admit zero owner kept explore dominates` gives `invalid`
- `no yes admit zero owner kept explore yes Dominates new` gives `invalid`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proof is about `judge`, the function the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.
